newsitem.title: USA: Police arrest 300 protestors at Yale.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest 300 protestors at Yale.

text.p: More than 300 demonstrators including AFL-CIO President John Sweeney were arrested on Tuesday evening during a peaceful protest outside the Yale University campus, police said.
Eyewitnesses estimated that 1,000 to 1,500 demonstrators marched through the streets of New Haven in support of two campus unions fighting to keep their jobs at the university.
The 312 arrested included Sweeney, New Haven Police Captain Roy Olson told Reuters. "They were arrested on the charge of creating a public disturbance, and all were given citations," said Olson.

In a statement released earlier Tuesday, Sweeney said, "The AFL-CIO will not stand still while Yale conducts a massive downsizing campaign aimed at nearly 4,000 clerical, technical, service and maintenance workers at the second- richest university."
Olson said all of the arrested -- who will have to pay a $88 fine within two weeks -- were released within two hours.
He could not confirm a radio report that Connecticut Secretary of State Miles Rappaport was also arrested.

"It was kind of bizarre," said a photographer at the scene. "They lined up in the middle of the intersection, and the cops came out with bullhorns and said, 'You have two minutes to disperse, or you will be rearrested for blocking the intersection."
The two Yale unions have been embroiled in difficult contract negotiations with the school since the autumn of 1995.
